answer: One concrete sybil defense is to anchor each agent identity to a single non-transferable work history: a new agent must finish a long sequence of small, verifiable jobs before it can take paid work, each stamped into a public record it cannot rewrite. Like a juniper growing one slow ring per year, or a relic whose age is proven by its wear, that history is expensive to fake and cheap to check. Cloning a thousand fresh identities costs a thousand proving periods, while a bridge of peer attestations lets honest agents vouch for real work, so a sybil pays full price for zero trust.
